subject: Cloud Computing
title: SLAs: The Uptime Promise
description: A micro-lesson that makes SLAs: The Uptime Promise usable.

hook.text: Cloud providers promise 99.99% uptime. That sounds perfect — but it still means 52 minutes of downtime a year.

buildup.text: Service Level Agreements spell out exactly how much uptime the provider guarantees.

discovery.text: If they miss the target, you get credits — not cash. Usually just a discount on next month's bill.

twist.text: SLA credits rarely cover real losses. An hour of downtime can cost a business millions in revenue.

climax.text: Smart teams design for failure, not uptime promises. SLAs are safety nets, not guarantees.

punchline.text: Don't trust the SLA. Design as if the cloud will fail — because it will.

quiz.question: What happens if a cloud provider misses its SLA uptime target?
options: Customers typically receive billing credits, not full compensation
The provider must pay for all business losses caused by downtime
Affected customers automatically receive free service for a year

details.summary: Service Level Agreements define the uptime cloud providers guarantee, typically 99.9% to 99.99% availability. When providers fail to meet their SLA, customers receive service credits. Understanding SLAs helps set realistic expectations and design architectures that exceed single-service guarantees.
details.whyItMatters: SLAs set the baseline for what reliability you can expect from cloud services. Designing for higher availability than any single SLA guarantees is essential for critical applications.
takeaways: Cloud SLAs typically guarantee 99.9% to 99.99% uptime
Violating an SLA results in service credits, not full refunds
Multi-service architectures compound SLA-related downtime risk

faq.question: How much downtime does a 99.9% SLA allow?
faq.answer: A 99.9 percent SLA allows about 8 hours and 45 minutes of downtime per year, or roughly 43 minutes per month. A 99.99 percent SLA allows only 52 minutes per year. Each additional nine reduces permitted downtime by a factor of ten.

faq.question: Do SLA credits cover business losses?
faq.answer: No. SLA credits typically cover 10 to 30 percent of the monthly bill for the affected service, not business losses from downtime. Organizations must design their own redundancy and carry business interruption insurance for critical applications.
